title: 1 Samuel Bible Quiz - Chapter 25
description: Ten questions on 1 Samuel 25: the death of Samuel, Nabal's insult and Abigail's wise intervention.

questions.explanation: Samuel died, and all Israel mourned for him and buried him at his house at Ramah.

questions.text: How many sheep did Nabal have?
questions.explanation: The man in Maon had three thousand sheep and a thousand goats.
Abigail was intelligent and had a beautiful face, but her husband was surly and evil in his doings.

answers.text: Proud, and quick to grow angry
Old, and very rich in flocks

questions.text: How many young men did David send to Nabal?
questions.explanation: David sent ten young men to go up to Carmel and greet Nabal in his name.

questions.text: About how many men followed David when he put on his sword?
questions.explanation: About four hundred men followed David, and two hundred stayed by the baggage.

questions.text: How did Nabal's young man describe David's men?
questions.explanation: The young man told Abigail, "They were a wall to us both by night and by day."

answers.text: "A wall to us both by night and by day"

questions.text: According to Abigail, what is with Nabal, just as his name says?
questions.explanation: Abigail said, "As his name is, so is he. Nabal is his name, and folly is with him."

questions.text: Why did Abigail tell Nabal nothing until the morning light?
questions.explanation: Nabal held a feast like the feast of a king, and his heart was merry, for he was very drunk.

answers.text: He was very drunk at a feast

questions.text: What happened to Nabal when his wife told him these things?
questions.explanation: When his wife told him these things, his heart died within him, and he became as a stone.

answers.text: His heart died within him, and he became as a stone
He laughed and mocked David again
He fled to the wilderness of Paran
He sent a gift to David

questions.text: To whom had Saul given Michal, David's wife?
questions.explanation: Saul had given Michal his daughter, David's wife, to Palti the son of Laish, who was of Gallim.
